question: does the level Pool 5 water surface measure one gen1 flight line's across-track coefficient on its own, without any other line?

inputs.role: raw 2008 gen1 LAZ tile holding the Mississippi Pool 5 backwater, vendor classification (9 = water)

params.name: dz_m
params.why: keeps class-9 returns within this distance of the line's modal water elevation, to exclude a second water body or a mis-classified bank; the effect of 0.15/0.30/0.60 m is measured and printed below

params.name: block_m
params.why: the 50 m cluster-robust block size used by swath_across_track_test.py

params.name: chunk
params.why: points per streamed read, a memory ceiling only; the reduction is done after the whole tile is assembled so it changes no result

columns.psid: point_source_id, i.e. the flight line, dimensionless integer
columns.dz_win: half-window about the modal water elevation, m
columns.n: class-9 water returns of that line inside the window
columns.blocks: independent 50 m spatial blocks they span
columns.x_span: easting span of those returns, m
columns.z_sd: standard deviation of the water-return elevation, m
columns.c_mm: OLS slope of elevation on tan(scan angle) within the line, mm per unit tangent -- the line's own across-track coefficient if the surface is level
columns.c_se: its cluster-robust standard error, mm per unit tangent
columns.h_sign: sign of the line's body-fixed side, from its heading (N-bound = +1)
columns.c_over_h: c_mm / (h_sign * h): the cross-track TILT the coefficient implies, mm/km. Common to all lines = the pool's own slope; differing = per-line roll
columns.dzdx: OLS slope of the water elevation on EASTING, mm/km: the pool surface slope as the lidar sees it, pooled over the line

headline: per-line across-track coefficient from a level Pool 5 water surface
